---
title: "How do I test whether two categories are associated?"
---

## What the question asks

How do I test whether two categories are associated?

## Steps in RStudio

1. Create a contingency table of observed counts.

2. Inspect expected counts from chisq.test().

3. Use the appropriate test and interpret p-value without implying causation.

## Runnable example

```{r}
counts <- matrix(c(24,15,18,27),nrow=2,byrow=TRUE,
                 dimnames=list(setting=c("A","B"),outcome=c("Yes","No")))
result <- chisq.test(counts,correct=FALSE)
print(counts)
print(result$expected)
print(result$p.value)
if (any(result$expected<5)) print(fisher.test(counts)$p.value)
```

## Interpret the result

The test asks whether the two categorical variables are independent in the sampled population under the sampling assumptions. It does not explain any observed association.

## Check before using real data

For sparse 2x2 tables, consider fisher.test(); expected-cell conditions and sampling design matter.
